content.title: ‘The Pitt’ season 2 complete release schedule: When is episode 13 dropping?
content.text: Home Entertainment Streaming ‘The Pitt’ season 2 complete release schedule: When is episode 13 dropping? Starring Noah Wyle, The Pitt returned for its second season on 8 January 2026, continuing its real-time emergency room format across a single high-pressure shift. Spanning 15-episodes in total, the second instalment premiered on HBO Max, with new episodes dropping every Thursday until the finale airs on 16 April 2026. In Hong Kong, the episodes are dropping a day later. The emergency department at the fictional Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Centre is once again under tremendous pressure and chaos as HBO’s hit medical drama, The Pitt, returns for season 2. Want more details? Keep scrolling to know everything about The Pitt season 2, from its plot and cast to the complete episode release schedule. The Emmy Award-winning medical series follows doctors, nurses and medical students in a high-pressure emergency department led by Dr Robby (played by Noah Wyle). Each season unfolds over one relentless day inside the hospital. Sharing how season 2 continues to mirror real life and real problems, lead actor Wyle told CBS NEWS, “People are going to lose their health insurance. People are going to delay care. People are going to continue to come in sicker. They’re going to be more volatile when they come in. That’s going to put more of a burden on staff. All this stuff is sort of moving towards this perfect storm of unsustainability.” How many episodes are there in The Pitt season 2? The new season consists of a total of 15 episodes. What is the duration of each episode? Each episode runs for approximately 55 to 60 minutes. Also read: Made in Korea complete release schedule Complete episode release schedule of The Pitt season 2 New episodes of the series are airing every Thursday on HBO Max. Viewers in Hong Kong can watch the episodes a day later. Below is the full episode release schedule of The Pitt season 2 for viewers in Hong Kong: Episode 1 – 9 January 2026 (Out now) Episode 2 – 16 January 2026 (Out now) Episode 3 – 23 January 2026 (Out now) Episode 4 – 30 January 2026 (Out now) Episode 5 – 6 February 2026 (Out now) Episode 6 – 13 February 2026 (Out now) Episode 7 – 20 February 2026 (Out now) Episode 8 – 27 February 2026 (Out now) Episode 9 – 6 March 2026 (Out now) Episode 10 – 13 March 2026 (Out now) Episode 11 – 20 March 2026 (Out now) Episode 12 – 27 March 2026 (Out now) Episode 13 – 3 April 2026 Episode 14 – 10 April 2026 Episode 15 (Finale) – 17 April 2026 Who is in the cast of season 2? Returning cast members for season 2 include Wyle as Dr Michael “Robby” Robinavitch, Supriya Ganesh as Dr Samira Mohan, Patrick Ball as Dr Frank Langdon, Katherine LaNasa as Dana Evans, Fiona Dourif as Dr Cassie McKay, Taylor Dearden as Dr Melissa “Mel” King, Isa Briones as Dr Trinity Santos, Gerran Howell as Dr Dennis Whitaker, Shabana Azeez as Dr Victoria Javadi, Amielynn Abellera as Perlah Alawi, Jalen Thomas Brooks as Mateo Diaz, Brandon Mendez Homer as Donnie Donahue, Kristin Villanueva as Princess, Ned Brower as Jesse Van Horn and Shawn Hatosy as Dr Jack Abbot. Season 2 also introduces a large slate of new cast members and characters. These include Sepideh Moafi as Dr Baran Al-Hashimi, Laëtitia Hollard as Emma, Lucas Iverson as James, Irene Choi as Joy, Charles Baker as Troy, Lawrence Robinson as Brian Hancock, Zack Morris as Jackson Davis, Brittany Allen as Roxie Hamler, Bonita Friedericy as Cora Wilkins, Taylor Handley as Paul Hamler, Jeff Kober as Duke, Meta Golding as Noelle Hastings, Luke Tennie as Dr Crus Henderson, Christopher Thornton as Dr Caleb Jefferson, Travis Van Winkle as Curtis Larson, Rusty Schwimmer as Monica Peters, Jayne Taini as Evelyn Bostick, Annabelle Toomey as Kylie Conners and Victor Rivas Rivers as Trent Norris. What is the plot of the new season? Season 2 is set around 10 months after the events of season 1 and unfolds entirely on 4 July, widely regarded as one of the busiest days of the year for emergency rooms due to fireworks injuries, alcohol-related incidents and heat exhaustion. Nurse Dana, now fully recovered, is back at the nurses’ station coordinating the department, and Dr Robby heads into his final shift before a three-month sabbatical — a planned motorcycle trip across North America that unsettles colleagues who routinely treat the aftermath of such crashes. The tension is quickly underscored when a motorcycle accident patient comes in; he wasn’t wearing a helmet. One key storyline follows the return of Dr Frank Langdon, who comes back to the ER on his first day after completing rehab for the substance misuse issues uncovered in season 1.
